API Testing
Complete E2E Guide (2026)

Master the backend. Learn how to validate communication between services, understand HTTP methods, secure endpoints, and automate your API tests with modern tools.

{/* Intro */}

1∩╕ÅΓâú What is an API? & What is API Testing?

API stands for Application Programming Interface. It acts as the messenger between the frontend UI and the backend database.

Example: You open the Amazon app Γ₧ö click "Search" Γ₧ö Frontend sends an API request to the server Γ₧ö Server returns the product list.

API Testing means testing the backend directly without the UI. We check if the Request, Response, Status Code, Data, Security, and Performance are completely correct.

{/* Why & Types of APIs */}

3∩╕ÅΓâú Why is it Important?

    {[ 'Faster than UI testing', 'Finds deep backend bugs early', 'Highly stable tests (less flaky)', 'Absolutely required for Microservices', 'Heavily used in CI/CD pipelines' ].map((step, i) => (

Modern 2026 apps are all API-driven.

4∩╕ÅΓâú Types of APIs

REST API (Most Popular)

Uses JSON format. Standard for web apps.

SOAP API

Uses strictly XML format. Common in legacy banking.

GraphQL API

Client specifically decides exactly what data fields to fetch.

{/* HTTP Methods & Status Codes */}

5∩╕ÅΓâú Core HTTP Concepts (Interview Heavy)

HTTP Methods

Method Usage
GETFetch data (e.g. GET /users)
POSTCreate data (e.g. POST /login)
PUTUpdate full data body
PATCHUpdate partial data fields
DELETEDelete data (e.g. DELETE /order/101)

Status Codes

Code Meaning
200 / 201Success / Created Successfully
400Bad Request (Invalid body/params)
401Unauthorized (Missing/Invalid Token)
403Forbidden (Token valid, lack permissions)
404Not Found (Wrong Endpoint)
500Server Error (Backend crashed)
{/* Breakdown & Flow */}

7∩╕ÅΓâú Anatomy of an API Request

https://api.shop.com /users?id=101
  • Base URL Γ₧ö api.shop.com
  • Endpoint Γ₧ö /users
  • Query Param Γ₧ö id=101
  • Headers: Metadata like Content-Type: application/json
  • Body: The actual JSON payload
  • Auth: Bearer tokens or API Keys

9∩╕ÅΓâú API Testing Process flow

1. Understand API docs (Swagger / OpenAPI)

2. Identify endpoints & prepare data

3. Send request & validate status code

4. Validate response JSON schema & exact Body

5. Validate response headers

6. Automate tests

7. Add to CI/CD pipelines

{/* Tools & Auth */}

≡ƒöƒ API Tools Hierarchy

Manual / Hybrid Tools

PostmanSoapUI

Most popular for creating collections & basic automation.

Code Automation Tools

RestAssuredKarateNewman

Java/JS based execution tailored for CI pipelines.

AI-Powered Testing (2026 Trend)

AI test case generation, auto-validation suggestions, intelligent self-healing, and deep AI bug log analysis.

1∩╕ÅΓâú1∩╕ÅΓâú Authentication Types

  • Basic Auth ΓÇö Plain Username & Password
  • Bearer Token ΓÇö Secure token-based (JWT) login
  • OAuth 2.0 ΓÇö Highly secure, 3rd party authorization
  • API Key ΓÇö Usually passed via Headers

1∩╕ÅΓâú2∩╕ÅΓâú What to perfectly validate?

Status Code Response Time Body Values JSON Schema Headers Error Messages
{/* Project Ideas */}

1∩╕ÅΓâú5∩╕ÅΓâú Real API Project Scenarios

Beginner

  • Test Login API flows
  • User CRUD operations
  • Validate basic error messages

Intermediate

  • E-commerce Order API workflow
  • Complex API Chaining (Login Γ₧ö Create Γ₧ö Get Γ₧ö Delete)
  • Strict Schema validation

Advanced

  • Microservices API testing
  • Consumer-Driven Contract testing
  • Massive Load testing APIs
  • Security & Header testing
{/* Best Practices */}

≡ƒôî 2026 Best Practices Summary

API Testing is a core skill. Modern architectures are exclusively microservice-based. Always perfectly validate both the code and the body payload. Utilize Environment Variables for multiple environments, heavily secure your tokens, always test the negative Error-handling paths, and deeply integrate the tests strictly inside your CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins / GitHub Actions).

≡ƒùä∩╕Å Database Testing Module

Database Testing
Complete E2E Guide (2026)

Master the backbone of modern apps. Learn SQL basics for QA, validate CRUD operations, guarantee data integrity, and confidently ensure UI payload matches DB reality.

{/* Intro & Why */}

1∩╕ÅΓâú What is Database Testing?

Database Testing strictly verifies that data is accurately stored, updated, and deleted without any silent corruption or structural mismatch between the UI inputs and the DB state.

Example Workflow:
User registers on website Γ₧ö QA directly queries the DB Γ₧ö
Is the exact user data row safely recorded in the `users` table?

3∩╕ÅΓâú Why it's Critical (2026 Reality)

  • Massive shifts toward complex Microservices.
  • Heavy reliance on automated real-time API integrations.
  • If the database is wrong Γ₧ö the entire system is critically wrong.
Catastrophe: User transfers $10,000 via UI. Code bug deducts $100,000 in the DB. (Instant Financial Disaster)
{/* Database Types */}

4∩╕ÅΓâú Types of Databases

Relational DB (RDBMS)

Highly structured data securely stored in strict relational tables with interconnected rows and columns.

PostgreSQL MySQL Oracle DB

NoSQL Database

Highly flexible, unstructured scaling data storage utilizing JSON document collections.

MongoDB DynamoDB Cassandra
{/* Test Types */}

5∩╕ÅΓâú DB Testing Architectures

Structural Testing

Validate exact table layouts, strict column variables, and overall schema map precision.

Functional Testing

Validate SQL Stored Procedures and automated Triggers execute correctly.

Data Validation

Verify payload data physically entered in the UI exactly mirrors DB physical rows.

Performance Tuning

Massive queries execute rapidly without stalling application threads.

Security Auditing

Unauthorized users cannot bypass APIs to access raw encrypted data stores.

ETL Testing

Extract, Transform, & Load. Flawless data migration into massive warehouses.

{/* Basic SQL & CRUD */}

6∩╕ÅΓâú Core SQL For Modern QA

SELECT (Fetch Data) SELECT * FROM users;
INSERT (Create Data) INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Vijay', 'v@test.com');
UPDATE (Modify Data) UPDATE users SET name='Vijay QA' WHERE id=101;
DELETE (Remove Data) DELETE FROM users WHERE email='v@test.com';

7∩╕ÅΓâú Master CRUD Validations

CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) is the absolute core of all API and Database Testing.

  • Γ£ö C: Submit signup via UI Γ₧ö Query DB Γ₧ö Record exists perfectly.
  • Γ£ö R: Ensure API heavily protected GET fetching reads actual data.
  • Γ£ö U: Change Profile Name Γ₧ö Query DB Γ₧ö Record mathematically updated.
  • Γ£ö D: Hard delete account Γ₧ö Query DB Γ₧ö Record completely vanished.

1∩╕ÅΓâú1∩╕ÅΓâú UI vs DB Mismatch Bug

User physically enters name = "Vijay" in the UI text box.
UI saves successfully and shows "Vijay".

> SELECT name FROM users WHERE id=101;
> RESULT: "Vijay Kumar"
Γ¥î CRITICAL FATAL: Data Payload Corrupted By Application Code in Transit.
{/* Data Integrity & Flow */}

8∩╕ÅΓâú Strict Data Integrity

  • Primary Key (PK): Force mathematical uniqueness. No duplicates ever allowed.
  • Foreign Key (FK) Integrity: An Order DB row CANNOT reference a User ID that does not exist.
  • NOT NULL Variables: Mandatory required app fields cannot physically be skipped.
  • Default Enums: Standardized states insert directly (e.g. status='PENDING').

1∩╕ÅΓâú2∩╕ÅΓâú Real Project Banking Flow

  1. Execute $500 Transfer physically in UI.
  2. Capture unique transaction hash/ID.
  3. Access backend using pgAdmin interface.
  4. Query UI ID matching `transaction_ledger` DB.
  5. Validate amount deducted perfectly minus fees.
  6. Validate receiver `balance` strictly updated.
{/* Automation & Tools */}

1∩╕ÅΓâú4∩╕ÅΓâú DB Automation Dominance (2026)

Manual SQL queries are too slow. Modern QA engineers automate SQL queries directly inside Cypress, Selenium, or RestAssured test frameworks.

1. Web UI Action: Click Submit button.
2. Automation: Script fires backend JDBC.
3. Execute: Database read immediately.
4. Assert: Expect UI value == DB returned value.

Intermediate

  • Automate DB connection in RestAssured API suites.
  • Write SQL JOINs to validate Foreign Keys.

Advanced

  • Deep Microservice sync db validations across distributed clouds.
  • Strict ETL massive migration verification scripts.

Security Testing
Complete E2E Guide (2026)

Defend applications against modern cyber threats. Master authentication, authorization, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, and standard security auditing practices for Web, Mobile, and API systems.

{/* Intro */}

1∩╕ÅΓâú What is Security Testing?

Security Testing ensures that confidential data is isolated, the strict integrity of the system is maintained, and unauthorized entities (hackers) cannot exploit logic gaps or vulnerabilities to extract data or bypass access rules.

Critical Violation:
If User A modifies a URL parameter from `id=101` to `id=102` and successfully views User B's banking details... This is a fatal Information Disclosure breach.

2∩╕ÅΓâú Why it's Critical in 2026

  • Modern apps instantly handle biometrics, massive cloud data lakes, and public Open-APIs.
  • Breaches result in catastrophic legal penalties (GDPR/CCPA) and permanent loss of public brand trust.
  • Equifax, Facebook, and massive global corporations have suffered catastrophic fallout from improperly tested auth rules.
{/* Security Types */}

3∩╕ÅΓâú Core Types of Security Audits

{[ { tag: 'Vulnerability Scan', desc: 'Running massive automated scanners against code syntax to identify known CVE gaps.', color: 'border-blue-500' }, { tag: 'Penetration Testing', desc: 'Simulating a targeted, malicious real-world "White Hat" hacker attack on specific endpoints.', color: 'border-red-500' }, { tag: 'Risk Assessment', desc: 'Identifying internal business logic risks, like weak password policies or untracked sensitive data.', color: 'border-yellow-500' }, { tag: 'Security Auditing', desc: 'A strict, deep compliance checklist verified line-by-line (e.g. PCI-DSS compliance).', color: 'border-green-500' }, { tag: 'Ethical Hacking', desc: 'Hiring heavily certified offensive engineers (CEH) to aggressively break the deployed system.', color: 'border-purple-500' }, ].map((el, i) => (

{el.tag}

{el.desc}

))}
{/* OWASP */}

4∩╕ÅΓâú The OWASP Top Web Risks

The Open Web Application Security Project strictly defines the most severe globally recorded vulnerabilities. Every QA must memorize these.

1. Broken Access Control: Users bypassing restricted URL routing rules.
2. Cryptographic Failures: Storing raw API keys or passwords in plaintext.
3. Injection (SQLi): Injecting raw malicious DB commands via UI inputs.
4. Insecure Design: Fundamentally weak architectural decisions.
5. Security Config Failure: Leaving default admin passwords on production DBs.
6. XSS (Cross-Site Scripting): Executing malicious JS payloads inside another user's browser view.
7. Auth Failures: Weak token TTL expiration allowing prolonged hijacked sessions.
{/* Auth Testing */}

5∩╕ÅΓâú Authentication Testing

"Identifying who the user actually is."

  • Strict Login success / Failure validations.
  • Validating rigorous password hash encryption formats.
  • Account locking behavior after 5 consecutive failed attempts.
  • Strict OTP (One Time Pass) generation and precise expiry thresholds.
  • Strict JWT session timeout termination rules.
Bug: Users circumventing the password field solely by pressing Enter on empty values.

6∩╕ÅΓâú Authorization Testing

"What is the authenticated user allowed to do?"

  • Normal free-tier users restricted from rendering Admin UI portals.
  • Preventing manual URL parameter manipulation for elevation of privilege.
  • API backend rejecting non-Admin tokens targeting administrative endpoints.
Bug: Standard user manually mutating URL schema to `/admin/dashboard` gracefully bypassing middleware protections.
{/* Domain specific security */}

7∩╕ÅΓâú Domain Specific Cyber Validation

Web Application Protocol

  • SQL Injection: Testing malicious payloads like `' OR 1=1 --` against login inputs to bypass authentication.
  • XSS (Cross-Site Scripting): Sinking `<script>alert('Hack')</script>` into User Profile comment blocks to observe payload execution.
  • CSRF: Verifying Cross-Site Request Forgery tokens strictly invalidate cross-origin malicious embedded form actions.
  • HTTPS Strictness: Confirming total isolation of insecure HTTP protocols and mixed content errors.

Mobile Architecture Security

  • Root/Jailbreak Sensors: Banking app must violently crash or lock if detecting Rooted OS states.
  • Keychain Encryption: Verifying local device caching is strictly fully encrypted and masked.
  • Static AST Scans: Validating zero hardcoded AWS or API secret keys exist inside compiled `.apk` binary files.
  • Biometric Fallbacks: Ensuring Fingerprint/FaceID scanners strictly hook into OS-level secure enclaves without local cache bypass logic.
{/* Automation & Tools */}

Manual / Tactical Break Scanners
Burp Suite Pro OWASP ZAP

Invaluable for intercepting active HTTP requests, forging payloads, sniffing API traffic, and executing automated SQLi injection spider crawling.

2.Manipulate local JWT claims locally, re-sign, and test for backend strict rejection.

Error: Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders

Effects are intended to synchronize state between React and external systems such as manually updating the DOM, state management libraries, or other platform APIs. In general, the body of an effect should do one or both of the following:
* Update external systems with the latest state from React.
* Subscribe for updates from some external system, calling setState in a callback function when external state changes.

Calling setState synchronously within an effect body causes cascading renders that can hurt performance, and is not recommended. (https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect).
